title: rcc-refcert: a Python research toolkit for structure-fair quantum circuit complexity
description:
rcc-refcert is a Python research toolkit for structure-fair quantum circuit complexity. It analyzes finite-control quantum models, verifies reference certificates and computes quantum circuit complexity lower bounds from exact target spectra or predeclared measurement counts. Researchers can also compare candidate preparations, use window RCC to compare subsystem complexity in pure and mixed states, and share complete calculations for independent verification.

The toolkit implements selected parts of Reference-Contingent Complexity (RCC), introduced in Structure-Fair Quantum Circuit Complexity: An Auditable Information-Theoretic Lower Bound.

Code and guides · Install from PyPI · Paper-to-code map

Understanding the cost of preparing a quantum state requires accounting for the resources already supplied by its physical background. The same state may be supplied by one background and require entropy removal and control in another. Structural fairness makes this distinction explicit: structure stably supplied by the background sets the reference zero point, while the operations and resources that generate additional target-directed structure are counted. Within an admissible model, RCC proves a rigorous lower bound on universal optimal quantum circuit complexity. Final-state information relative to the reference bounds the cost of every successful preparation history, without reconstructing how the state was produced.

Research tasks

  • Models and reference certificates. Define quantum channels, reference states, control rules and resource assignments. Analyze terminating program outputs, prepare certificate candidates for stable finite models, and independently verify reference certificates and local gain–cost conditions.
  • Complexity lower bounds. Use complete exact target spectra or predeclared fixed-projector measurement counts to calculate a terminal-state certificate and the resulting preparation-cost lower bound.
  • Preparation costs. Check candidate programs against complete targets, compare costs and scan accuracy requirements. Exact diagonal-preserving recipes combine verified gain exclusions with feasible preparations to give rigorous cost intervals; numerical matrix models support candidate diagnostics.
  • Window RCC. Compare subsystem complexity in pure and mixed states, analyze local and correlation contributions under a common reference and control bandwidth, and follow these quantities along a preparation.
  • Independent verification. Save model, certificate, cost and window calculations with their inputs and results. Another researcher can recompute the analysis from the saved bundle and compare fresh evidence with the original results.
  • Reproduce paper calculations. Rerun the bundled RCC reference calculations and compare their results with frozen evidence. The paper-to-code map locates the implemented definitions and equations.

Examples and guides

Worked examples connect a qubit's one-slot lower bound to a matching reset and examine four-qubit reset and algorithmic-cooling tasks. State-comparison probes contrast paired Bell and GHZ states and study phase noise and cooling trajectories. Editable inputs and three Jupyter tutorials help researchers adapt these calculations to their own tasks.

For a first complete calculation, follow the worked lower-bound example from its physical model to a matching preparation. The research-task links above lead to guides for adapting each workflow.

Run and share a calculation

Python and command-line interfaces support all these workflows. With Python 3.10 or later, install this version and run an editable reset example in a new working directory:

python -m pip install "rcc-refcert==0.3.0"
python -m rcc_refcert cost template cyclic-reset > task.json
python -m rcc_refcert cost analyze task.json --bundle task.rccbundle

Expect a preparation-cost interval of [5,5] atomic slots: a lower bound of five and a successful five-slot program, including the halt operation. Edit task.json to change the inputs and rerun the calculation. The saved bundle contains the inputs and original results; recompute it independently with:

python -m rcc_refcert bundle verify task.rccbundle

To reproduce the bundled paper calculations and check them against the frozen reference evidence, run:

python -m rcc_refcert reproduce --check

Expect three MATCH checks, for the reference expectations, data and report. The reference-case guide explains each case and its intended scientific outcome.

Cost and window reports support text, JSON and Markdown; window profiles also export to CSV and optional plots. The recipient guide explains shared evidence and compatibility.

Interpreting the results

Exact recipe-based cost intervals refer to the declared model, complete target, tolerance and atomic cost. Matrix checks and numerical candidate diagnostics retain their numerical evidence level. Window RCC uses a declared reference and resource scale to compare state-side complexity; a full finite-accuracy cost bound also uses the model inputs and one-shot corrections. Definitions, units and physical assumptions are explained in the scientific scope and the task guides.

The RCC paper also discusses connections to high-energy physics: its generation-cost lower bounds can be compared with geometric proposals for boundary-state complexity, including the complexity–volume and complexity–action conjectures, when the preparation task and resource conventions are aligned.

Version 0.3.0 adds preparation-cost intervals, subsystem complexity profiles and independently verifiable workflow bundles to the model, certificate and terminal-state tools. See the changelog for changes and compatibility notes.
notes: If you use this software in your research, please cite the software version used and the associated RCC paper.
